title: Add Two Small Integers
statement:
Given two integers a and b, return their sum a + b.

This is a warm-up: it checks that you can read the inputs, keep the signs right and return the value in the expected shape.

examples.why: Adding a smaller positive number to a negative one stays negative.

hints: There is no trick: the language's + operator is exactly what you need.
Check the sign cases: negative plus positive, two negatives, and zero.
If an interviewer forbids +, see the bitwise version: XOR adds without carries and AND shifted left gives the carries.

explain.intuition:
The sum of two small integers fits comfortably in any number type, so a + b is the whole answer. Problems like this exist to test your setup: reading parameters, returning the right type, and not mixing up strings and numbers (in JavaScript, "8" + 34 is "834").

The interesting version forbids the plus operator. Then a ^ b adds every bit position without carrying, and (a & b) << 1 is the carry. Repeat until the carry is zero.
steps: Bit version: while b is not 0, compute carry = (a & b) << 1, set a = a ^ b, then b = carry. Return a.
pitfalls: Adding values that arrived as strings, which concatenates instead of adding.
In the bitwise version in Python, negative numbers have no fixed width, so the loop never ends without a 32-bit mask.

solutions.title: Use the + operator
solutions.idea: The values are small, so the built-in addition is exact.

solutions.title: Add with bit operations
solutions.idea: XOR is addition without carries; AND shifted left is the carry. Repeat until no carry is left.
